sections.title: About Togo
sections.content: Togo, officially the Togolese Republic, is a country in West Africa. It is bordered by Ghana to the west, Benin to the east and Burkina Faso to the north. It is one of the least developed countries in the world. It extends north from the Gulf of Guinea to the Burkina Faso-Togo border. It is a small, tropical country, spanning 57,000 square kilometres with a population of approximately 8 million. It has a width of less than 115 km (71 mi) between Ghana and its eastern neighbour Benin.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Are Observed in Togo
sections.content: On public holidays, government offices and public schools are closed, and banks/financial institutions typically close. Private businesses may operate reduced hours. Travel activity often increases around major religious and national holidays.

sections.title: Why Togoâ€™s Public Holidays Matter
sections.content: Knowing Togoâ€™s public holidays helps with business planning and payroll management, school and academic scheduling, and travel/accommodation planning. Both residents and visitors benefit from understanding when services may be unavailable.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Togo?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Togo?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Togo?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Togo?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Togo?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
